13.t: Working with data: does it conduct?
q: Sodium chloride dissolved and molten (pure water only very slightly).
Explain why sodium chloride conducts only when molten or dissolved.
The ions must be free to move to carry charge; in the solid they are fixed in the lattice.
Sugar solution did not conduct. What does this tell you about sugar?
Sugar has no ions: it is made of covalent molecules, which do not carry charge when dissolved.
